comment: **Not a measurement yet: the input it would measure is missing.**
The plan was to measure a symbol being found from its own doc comment, which is a query set written by the code's
authors rather than by a reviewer - the thing 'no recorded query set with committed expected results' was actually
blocking. **The corpus has the comments** (672 JSDoc-annotated exported declarations across `packages/`) and **the
graph has the field** (`GraphNode.docstring`), and the two never meet:
blockedBy: doc comments reach the graph for typescript only; javascript builds captures inline, python uses string literals, and the remaining providers are unexamined

evidence.andWhatTheCorpusHas: 672 JSDoc-annotated exported declarations across packages/, counted with a regex over the files

andThisIsTheSecondCapabilityThatNeverWor: `tools` returned `failed` on every corpus since it was written - a regex with no capture group, read from `match[1]!` under a comment claiming the group was not optional.
`docstring` is `null` on every node in every language - so symbol documentation is not extracted at all, and anything that would use it has been empty from the start.
Both were invisible from outside: `tools` was one word - `partial` - in a result nobody read, and an empty docstring looks the same as a symbol that has none.
andTheAssertionThatCaughtIt: The harness asserted that it had at least one query before computing a recall figure. **Without that line it would have reported a recall over zero queries** - a division with no error, in a file that would have looked like a measurement.
next: Extract doc comments in the language providers, then this measurement has an input. Until then the semantic-search-accuracy row is blocked on something more basic than a query set: the descriptions exist in the source and are not in the graph.

andAnAttemptMovesItWithoutClosingIt.whatWasChanged: The base provider now carries a comment forward to the declaration under it: a walk sees a comment immediately before the declaration it belongs to, so a field holding the last comment and consumed by the next capture is the whole association. The field resets per file.
andWhyNoLanguageBenefitsYet: **Typescript and javascript override `walkAndCapture`**, and their overrides call a private `buildCapture` rather than the base `emitCapture` - so the consumption there never runs. **A base-class change does not reach a subclass that replaced the method it lives in**, which is worth writing down once: it is the reason this fix is inert for the two languages it was written for.

**Python docstrings are string literals, not comments.** A `"""..."""` immediately inside a `def` is an expression statement, so a comment-based association has nothing to associate. **That is a second mechanism, not a bug in the first.**
andAnAttemptMovesItWithoutClosingIt.andWhatIsLeft: A `pendingDocComment` field and the consumption on the base path, which is correct and reaches no language today. **The next step is per-provider work**: typescript, javascript and any other override needs the same consumption in its own capture path, and python needs string-literal docstrings rather than comments. **The field is left in place because the mechanism is right and the remaining work is one line in each overriding provider.**
andAnAttemptMovesItWithoutClosingIt.andWhatWasNotDone: **No test was committed red.** The failing test was removed, so the failure is recorded here rather than in the suite - because a red suite blocks everything else, and this is one capability rather than the whole build.

andItNowWorksForTypeScript.whatChanged: The consumption moved out of `emitCapture` and into `attachDocComment`, **a method any walk can call** - because a base-class change does not reach a subclass that replaced the method it lives in, and typescript and javascript both replace `walkAndCapture`. The typescript provider's `buildCapture` now calls it, and that is its only capture path.
andItNowWorksForTypeScript.result: kineticEnergy gets its JSDoc and undocumented gets an empty string, which is the association and not just the text
andItNowWorksForTypeScript.theGuard: packages/analyzer/src/languages/__tests__/docstring-extraction.test.ts, which asserts the prose arrives without its comment syntax, that a comment does not land on the symbol after the one it describes, that the single-line form works as well as the block form, and that exactly one symbol carries it
andWhatIsStillMissing: **Javascript** overrides `walkAndCapture` and builds its captures inline rather than through a helper, so it has no single place to call `attachDocComment` - **the same call, at several sites**.
**Python** docstrings are string literals rather than comments, so the comment mechanism cannot reach them at all. **That is the second mechanism, still unbuilt.**
**The other thirty-one providers** were not examined: some will inherit the base path and work already, and some will override the walk like typescript does.
